items.title: Federal Court Halts Pregnant Workers’ Protection Law
items.author: Coral Davenport
items.content: <article>The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals said the law was unconstitutional because it was passed with proxy voting during the Covid pandemic. It is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court.</article>

items.title: It’s a Bill on Energy Permits, but Trump’s Pet Projects Are Part of the Debate
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>The pervasive presence of the president hovers over the bipartisan legislation to speed up construction of energy projects that are advancing through Congress.</article>

items.title: Takeaways From Trump’s Post-Trip News Conference
items.author: Erica L. Green
items.content: <article>President Trump called the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China an “amazing event.” He also said he would work with Democrats in Congress on key issues.</article>

items.title: Officials Find Cascade of Problems With ICE Training in Trump’s Immigration Crackdown
items.author: Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>In a draft report, officials found widespread training gaps as the Department of Homeland Security sought to rapidly hire and deploy 10,000 new officers.</article>

items.title: Trump Flaunts Camaraderie With Xi and Putin but Has Little to Show for It
items.author: Katie Rogers and David E. Sanger
items.content: <article>President Trump called Russia’s leader his “friend” and marveled at China’s warm welcome for his first-ever trilateral summit. But there were no breakthroughs on nuclear control, the war in Ukraine or A.I.</article>

items.title: On the Carpet of Melania Trump’s Amazon Premiere in New York
items.author: Sandra E. Garcia
items.content: <article>Ten months after the premiere of her Amazon documentary in Washington, the first lady debuted a follow-up series far from her husband’s seat of power.</article>

items.title: Top White House Cybersecurity Official Is Replaced
items.author: Chris Cameron and Dustin Volz
items.content: <article>The departure of Sean Cairncross comes after a series of technological outages affected U.S. companies and federal agencies in the past week.</article>

items.title: Here’s the latest.
items.author: Erica L. Green, Shawn McCreesh, Michael Crowley and Julian E. Barnes

items.title: Fact-Checking Trump’s News Conference After His Asia Trip
items.author: Linda Qiu
items.content: <article>President Trump repeated and revised a number of falsehoods and exaggerations during a news conference.</article>

items.title: Ron DeSantis Ponders a Presidential Run in a Post-Trump World
items.author: Patricia Mazzei
items.content: <article>In a wide-ranging interview, the governor of Florida talked about the potential timing of a presidential run. “I haven’t made any decisions,” he said.</article>

items.title: Takeaways From ‘Melania: The Series,’ a Coda to the Film on the First Lady
items.author: Melena Ryzik
items.content: <article>A streaming sequel to the documentary that was released in January follows Melania Trump in the days after her husband’s second inauguration.</article>

items.title: Agriculture Secretary’s Christian Messages to Staff Went ‘Too Far,’ Judge Says
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>A federal judge ordered limits on Brooke Rollins’s promotion of her religious beliefs, saying her emails to her department had violated the First Amendment.</article>

items.title: C.F.T.C. Officials Considered Investigating Trump’s Memecoin, Then Punted
items.author: Sharon LaFraniere
items.content: <article>Lawyers at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission looked into possible fraud soon after the digital token’s launch, then decided they would not get the commission’s support.</article>

items.title: Justice Department Gives Up on Alaska Senate Lawsuit
items.author: Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>The Trump administration had sought to block certification of election results if Senator Dan Sullivan, a Republican, lost narrowly in his bid for re-election. Critics had called the suit meritless.</article>

items.title: What Trump, Putin and Xi Left on the Table
items.author: Natalie Kitroeff, David E. Sanger, Michael Simon Johnson, Caitlin O’Keefe, Carlos Prieto, Annie Minoff, Paige Cowett, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>A summit among the leaders of the United States, China and Russia produced no treaties on war or nuclear weapons — and the A.I. race wasn’t even on the agenda.</article>

items.title: Former Biden Chief, With Help From Alex Soros, Will Gather Aides of 2028 Hopefuls
items.author: Reid J. Epstein and Tyler Pager
items.content: <article>Jen O’Malley Dillon, who led the former president’s last two White House bids, is inviting top Democratic operatives to a gathering funded in part by the megadonor Alex Soros.</article>

items.title: Elon Musk Backs Away From MAGA and the Trump Presidency He Shaped
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>The man who helped elect President Trump in 2024 and led DOGE is trying to rewrite history.</article>

items.title: Senate Republicans Block Bid to Rein in Trump on Iran War
items.author: Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>In the first vote on the conflict since the midterm elections, most in the G.O.P. banded together against placing any limits on a conflict that voters repudiated at the polls.</article>
